note: Every string the engine can draw. If a string is not here or in a room, dialogue or menu file, the engine cannot render it. Harness values are placeholders, not written content.

sentence.note: itemTemplate and itemOnly are new with the inventory. They are interface grammar of the same class as the two above them, not written content -- no document specifies them because no document specifies '{verb} {target}' either.

hud.note: The key-hint line is gone. There are no required keys: the MENU button in the panel is the route to save, load, options and quit. Chromebook top-row keys are browser keys and never reached the game.

map.note: Interface grammar, not written content -- the same class as the sentence templates. Doc 20 names the screen THE MAP and specifies that its labels are drawn by the engine in the game font.

timing.note: How long a line stays up. Interface grammar of the same class as the sentence templates -- no document specifies it because no document specifies '{verb} {target}' either. It is HERE rather than in a .ts file because it is a number a person will want to change after watching the opening, and because menu.json already declares an unimplemented OPTIONS item called 'Text speed': when that is built, this is the value it scales, and a rate buried in the engine could not be.
timing.actCardNote: Added to doc 17 beat 7's stated ~3s, so the card holds about seven seconds. The doc's number is how long the BEAT lasts; this is how long two lines of a 5x7 font take to read, which is interface timing and not something doc 17 should have to state. Raised twice from watching it: 2 answered 'too fast' from the deployed build, where the card had exactly the beat's three seconds and one line of text, and 4 is the ruling after a proper play-through. It lives here so the next correction is a number in a content file rather than a rebuild. LOWERED TO 2 after a further play-through: at 4 the card held about seven seconds and read as a pause rather than a title. Two puts it near five, which is still above the three the beat states and above the 2 that once answered 'too fast' -- the difference is that 2 was measured against ONE line of text and the card now carries two.
timing.holdNote:
DOC 30 SECTION 4.1's BINDING FORMULA, and section 13's constants: readingHold = clamp(1.8s, 8.0s, 0.45s + visibleGlyphs x 0.055s). It is now the ONLY reading hold, and it governs a scripted line, a dialogue utterance and a bark alike -- which is what doc 30 section 4.1 asks for when it says one timing service owns all three.

There was no such number for dialogue and that is why a conversation read as a menu: interactive dialogue waited for a click FOREVER, so every line was a prompt rather than a performance.

IT REPLACED A SECOND SET AND THAT IS A RETIME. lineSecondsPerGlyph 0.045 and lineSecondsMinimum 1.6 were what the sequence runner used and what the opening was watched and tuned against. Errata 61 recorded the split as deliberate and said what merging it would cost -- 'a retune of the opening, watched, not a refactor'. Merged, every one of the opening's fifteen lines gets longer and none gets shorter: 25.9 seconds of speech becomes 31.2. The longest line in the opening is 73 glyphs, 3.28s before and 4.46s now, so the 8-second ceiling never fires there and the whole difference is the base and the rate. If the opening now drags, these four numbers are where it is fixed.

fullscreen.note: Interface grammar, the same class as the map's. Two words rather than one because the button is a TOGGLE and has to say which way it goes -- 'FULL' when windowed, 'WINDOW' when full. Both fit the 336-unit cell at the scaled face: six glyphs is 216 units.
